note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for rising PSA and prior negative biopsy to discuss management options.

Recently retired truck driver with a history of coronary artery disease and chronic kidney disease. He lives alone but is supported by his spouse, who is his primary contact. He consumes approximately 8 units of alcohol weekly and leads a sedentary lifestyle with occasional walking. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 10/35. He is currently taking aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol. He has no known drug allergies. He attends regular dental check-ups and visits the pain clinic for chronic shoulder pain. He has a history of smoking but quit in 2005 after 17 pack-years.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth and non-tender with no palpable nodules, consistent with cT1c staging. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs and no signs of acute distress. Visual impairment is noted, and large-print correspondence has been requested.
